description: The scenes both rigs draw from the fixtures, by the same names: tests/parity/desktop.py for Baude, android/.../screenshots/Parity.kt for the phone. chat scenes open fixtures/sessions.json's first session, or the `session`th (from 0), with only the first `lines` lines of its transcript (all of them when absent), or of the fixture named by `transcript` instead; a session whose state is `working` is shown at a turn; `files` names a folder of fixtures/ whose contents join the chat's folder; `transcript` (a fixtures file used for the first session instead of sessions.json's), `state` (the first session's state as its host lists it, for the phone) and `ask` (the tool_use id of a call in the transcript to ask permission for) are further optional keys of a chat scene; `open` opens every tool call's input and output where the app can. `bots` (a fixtures file of two chats made Bots, one on a host that is gone: the list and the chat shown from it instead of sessions.json) is a further key of a home or chat scene; `threads` (a fixtures file of chats on two hosts that are up, some started by a Bot on the other, each on the host its `on` names) one of a home scene, with `pick` the host whose chats are listed (the fixture's first, without) and `bot`: `trashed` or `archived`, the Bot (the fixture's first chat) deleted or archived on its host (a deleted one stays so: that scene is last). `inventory` names the schema/ui entries the scene shows. `running` (background tasks heard as started), `process` (a Processes row: opened, or with `full` its page), `subagents` (a fixtures folder of the first session's subagents' transcripts), `view` (a subagent's View), `reveal` (a folder link of the chat's folder), `gallery` (that folder's gallery, from its tree row) and `hold` (a Files row's menu) are further optional keys of a panel or chat scene. `signal` (a fixtures file of the names the folder's Signal glossary has), `card` (a name whose card the Signal page shows), `ref` (a name in a reply to tap) and `signal_menu` (the header's Signal popover open) are the Signal scenes' further keys. `typed` is typed into the box a character at a time, `cut` shows the chat's last turn cut short by a restart, and `lightbox` opens the chat's first picture in the large view, `zoom` then double-taps the middle of the screen and `swipe` then drags a finger leftwards that fraction of the screen's width and holds it there (the phone only); `open` also opens every compaction's summary, and `into` then scrolls the chat to the first one's heading, that many px above the chat's top (below it when negative). `git` makes the chat's folder the fixture repository (tests/parity/gitfixture.py) and sets its Git page (`pick`: the branches picked, `every`: every branch, `branches`: the branch list open, `commit`: the card of the commit with that subject), and `github` has gh signed in, with fixtures/github.json. `inventory` names the schema/ui entries the scene shows. `running` (background tasks heard as started), `process` (a Processes row: opened, or with `full` its page), `subagents` (a fixtures folder of the first session's subagents' transcripts), `view` (a subagent's View), `reveal` (a folder link of the chat's folder), `gallery` (that folder's gallery, from its tree row) and `hold` (a Files row's menu) are further optional keys of a panel or chat scene. `signal` (a fixtures file of the names the folder's Signal glossary has), `card` (a name whose card the Signal page shows), `ref` (a name in a reply to tap) and `signal_menu` (the header's Signal popover open) are the Signal scenes' further keys.
